title: bug: doctor run from WSL reports a live Windows daemon's daemon.json as stale, because it checks the Windows pid with kill -0, which WSL cannot see. TROUBLESHOOTING.md's "daemon.json is stale" fix then says rm .moe/daemon.json, so a WSL agent-mode seat that follows doctor deletes the live daemon's discovery file
description:
Hunt #17 (task-3488566e) found this as held item (a). It was re-run read-only from WSL at bb0bc17e on 2026-11-04; the evidence is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-3488566e/mine/doctor-wsl-foreign-live.txt.
- `node <snapshot>/packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js doctor --project /mnt/d/projexts/moes` prints `[WARN] daemon.json: daemon.json present but pid 36176 not running (stale)` and exits 0.
- daemon.json holds pid 36176, port 9876, bindHost wsl and projectPath D:/projexts/moes, so it is a Windows-owned record.
- In WSL, `kill -0 36176` gives "No such process".
- `curl http://172.26.208.1:9876/health` (the WSL gateway) answers healthy, with pid 36176 and projectPath D:/projexts/moes.

Cause: packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.ts:99-107 decides liveness with isProcessAlive(parsed.pid) alone. index.ts already handles a foreign record: isForeignDaemonInfo (:97), wslGatewayHost (:122), and validateDaemonInfoForProject (:357-380), which probes /health over loopback and then the WSL gateway. The launchers' sh pre-flight does the same, and it refuses to delete daemon.json when the probe fails. doctor reuses none of this.

Harm: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:75-82 ("daemon.json is stale", then `rm .moe/daemon.json`) has no liveness check. This repo runs in WSL agent mode, so following doctor's advice there deletes the live daemon's daemon.json. New proxies then cannot find the port, and a later start may launch a second daemon on the same .moe/.

Fix direction:
- For a foreign record (isForeignDaemonInfo), doctor's daemon.json probe asks /health over loopback, then over the WSL gateway.
- A reply whose projectPath is this project counts as alive: report pass and name the host that answered.
- Report stale only when no /health answers.
- In TROUBLESHOOTING's stale section, tell the reader to confirm /health does not answer before removing daemon.json, checking the WSL gateway too when in WSL, and never to remove it while /health answers.

Sequencing: this row depends on task-78fa7110 (relative --project), whose fix is expected to touch index.ts's foreign-daemon helpers. Plan against its landed shape and re-anchor the line numbers above.

Placement: task-3950184e also edits doctor.test.ts and TROUBLESHOOTING.md (around rows 1254-1255). Put this row's tests in their own describe block and edit only the stale section. No dependency edge is needed in worktree mode.
definitionOfDone: From WSL, take a daemon.json whose projectPath is a drive-letter path while a /health reporting the same project answers on loopback or the WSL gateway. Doctor's daemon.json probe must not report 'not running (stale)': it reports the daemon live and names the host that answered. A regression test in doctor.test.ts covers this foreign-live case with a stubbed health server, and a foreign-dead case (no /health answers) still warns stale.

The 'daemon.json is stale' section of docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md tells the reader to confirm /health does not answer before removing daemon.json, checking the WSL gateway as well when in WSL, as the launchers do. It also says never to remove daemon.json while /health answers.
The daemon tests for the touched files pass (doctor.test.ts, plus a test of any helper this row moves or shares), tsc is clean, and npm run lint passes at the repo root.

implementationPlan.description: doctor judges a foreign record by /health alone (packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.ts; transcribe the prototype hunk with the Edit tool). Import foreignProbeHosts and isForeignDaemonInfo. probeDaemonJson gains expectedProjectPath (runDoctor passes projectPath). When `typeof parsed.projectPath === 'string' && isForeignDaemonInfo({ projectPath })` holds, it returns probeForeignDaemonJson(port, pid, bindHost, expectedProjectPath) BEFORE isProcessAlive. A non-string projectPath is never foreign, because RegExp.test would coerce ['D:/x']. Extract endpoint(host, port) (IPv6 bracketed) and judgeHealthBody(body, where, expectedProjectPath, pid) out of probeDaemonReachability with byte-identical messages, so every local row and doctor.bindHost.test.ts B1-B5 stay unchanged. probeForeignDaemonJson asks each foreignProbeHosts address in order with probeHealth: no HTTP answer (statusCode undefined: refused, timed out, not HTTP) -> next address; a 200 JSON body -> judgeHealthBody; any other HTTP answer (503 from a live but unhealthy daemon, index.ts:767; 403; unparseable) -> warn '<where> answered but /health did not confirm a healthy Moe daemon (<error or HTTP n>)'. The first pass wins: '[OK] daemon.json valid: written on the other side of the WSL boundary (pid N, port P); /health answered on <where>', with that pass as the reachability line. Otherwise the first answer's verdict becomes the reachability line, and daemon.json warns '... /health on <where> answered but did not confirm this daemon'. Only when no address answers: '[WARN] ... no /health answered on <every endpoint asked, or a no-address reason> (stale)' and no reachability line. DaemonJsonProbe gains `foreignReachability?: ProbeResult | null`, which probeDaemonReachability returns first, so a foreign record is never re-dialed at the recorded loopback. error handling: probeHealth resolves an outcome on every error, timeout and oversize body, and foreignProbeHosts never throws. doctor still never signals, deletes or writes anything.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: `moe-daemon doctor` judges a daemon.json written on the other side of the WSL boundary (isForeignDaemonInfo) by /health alone. It asks the addresses the daemon lifecycle asks (foreignProbeHosts: the recorded bindHost when it is this machine, then the WSL gateway on Linux). An answer confirming this daemon is reported live, naming the endpoint that answered. Any other HTTP answer is reported as the local probe would judge it, never as stale. It warns stale only when no address answers. TROUBLESHOOTING's stale section tells the reader to confirm /health does not answer (loopback or bindHost, plus the WSL gateway in WSL) before removing daemon.json, and never to remove it while /health answers for this project.
acceptanceCriteria: F1: a foreign record whose /health answers on loopback gives '[OK] daemon.json:' naming 127.0.0.1:<port>, never 'not running' or 'stale', and exit 0, though its pid is not alive here.
F2 (Linux): the WSL gateway's answer for this project beats loopback's answer for another project; both lines name the gateway endpoint.
F3: with no answer, it warns '(stale)' naming the endpoints asked, adds no reachability line and exits 0, whether or not the pid number is alive here.
F4: an answer only for another project is never green and exits 1. F5: a 503 answer for this project is never called stale.
Local-record doctor output and index.ts lifecycle behavior are unchanged (doctor.test.ts reachability rows, doctor.bindHost.test.ts B1-B5, index.test.ts X2-X8 and B5 pass unedited).
invariants: doctor never signals, deletes or writes anything.
A repository-derived bindHost is dialed only when isLocalAddress holds.
A foreign record is never judged by process.kill.
process.platform is read at call time.
compatibility: No MCP tool contract or daemon.json format change.
